results.title: Samson Awiah elected Ghana Cricket Association President, pledges nationwide representation
results.content: Awiah polled 11 votes out of 25 valid ballots cast at the elective congress held last Saturday at the Cantonments Police Station Mosque in Accra. Incumbent Emmanuel Owusu-Ansah Asare garnered nine votes, while Prince Eugene King managed five.

results.title: Go Church Belgium documentary: What viewers were not told about two former Lighthouse bishops
results.content: The Belgian documentary investigating Go Church has raised serious allegations concerning Bishop Dag Heward-Mills and Lighthouse Chapel International. Those claims deserve examination. So does the background of the people making them. Emmanuel Oko Mensah and Lawrence Odonkor once held senior positions in Lighthouse. Both now criticise its leadership. Here are three pieces of context viewers should consider before reaching conclusions.

results.title: NACOC Director-General urges journalists to investigate drug trafficking networks in Ghana
results.content: The Director-General of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), Major General Maxwell Obuba Mantey, has challenged journalists to investigate the networks and vulnerabilities that enable drug trafficking rather than focusing mainly on arrests and drug seizures. He said deeper media investigations into how trafficking networks operate and the gaps they exploit could improve public understanding of the narcotics trade and strengthen efforts to protect vulnerable communities. The Ashanti Regional Director of NACOC, Rees Hakeem Oduro, delivered the message on behalf of the Director-General at the Ashanti Media Excellence Awards in Kumasi.

results.title: JoyNews’ Nana Boakye Yiadom wins Community Impact Journalism Award; two others at Ashanti GJA Awards
results.content: JoyNews journalist Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom has won the Best in Community Impact Journalism award at the 2025 Ashanti Regional Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Awards, alongside two other recognitions for his work in environmental and health journalism. He won the top award with his investigative documentary, Deadly Doses – Unmasking Ghana’s Drug Epidemic, which examined the growing challenge of substance abuse and its devastating effects on individuals and communities. The documentary explored the realities of drug use, particularly among young people, highlighting the social and health consequences of addiction while drawing attention to the need for effective interventions.

results.title: MMDAs directed to maintain Nissan Patrol vehicles for Traditional Councils
results.content: The Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs has directed Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) in possession of Nissan Patrol four-wheel-drive vehicles to maintain them in good working condition for use by Traditional Councils within their respective jurisdictions. In a directive dated October 22, the Chief Director, Amin Abdul-Rahaman, said the Minister had instructed the Assemblies to ensure the vehicles were maintained to facilitate traditional authorities’ official movements and engagements.

results.title: Bright Simons proposes $13m civil service AI assistant as alternative to Ghana’s $270m GhanaChat plan
results.content: Vice-President and head of Research at the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education, Bright Simons has proposed a cheaper alternative to Ghana’s planned US$270 million GhanaChat project, arguing that a sovereign artificial intelligence (AI) assistant for the civil service could be a more practical starting point for the country’s AI ambitions. In a post on X, Mr Simons questioned the rationale for developing a national AI platform to compete with global services such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude when existing models could potentially support government operations at a lower cost.

results.title: GhanaChat data centre could require $61m annual subsidy – Bright Simons
results.content: Vice-President and head of Research at the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education, Bright Simons has questioned the financial viability of Ghana’s proposed US$270 million artificial intelligence (AI) data centre, warning that its operating costs could require substantial annual government subsidies. In an analysis published on X, Mr Simons said the facility, which is expected to support the development and hosting of GhanaChat, would have a computing capacity of about 2,100 graphics processing units (GPUs) and an information technology (IT) load of 4.3 megawatts (MW). He said this would add the equivalent of about 90 per cent of Ghana’s entire commercial data centre load in 2024, estimated at 4.8 MW.

results.title: Bright Simons flags computing capacity error in Ghana’s AI strategy and questions GhanaChat costs
results.content: Vice-President and head of Research at the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education, Bright Simons, has raised concerns about Ghana’s national artificial intelligence (AI) strategy, pointing to what he calls a critical mathematical error in its computing capacity targets and questioning the feasibility of its infrastructure and cost projections. Referring to an argument he made on Joy News’ Digital Economy Forum on AI and the Ghana Economy on Wednesday, Mr Simons said in a post on X that the strategy lists Ghana’s computing capacity target for 2027 as “1021 FLOPS” and the 2035 target as “1025 FLOPS”.

results.title: TOR eyes stock market listing as it tackles $517m debt
results.content: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) is considering a listing on the Ghana Stock Exchange as management seeks fresh investment while pursuing the restructuring of an inherited debt burden of approximately $517 million.

results.title: Include private universities in national funding plans — Catholic University VC tells gov’t
results.content: The Vice-Chancellor of the Catholic University of Ghana (CUG), Prof. Matthew Glover Addo, has urged the government to establish a dedicated fund to support private universities, warning that current interventions for first-year students in public universities could undermine enrolment prospects in the private tertiary education sector.

results.title: Africa must move youth-led green innovations beyond ideas to viable businesses – Ahmed Bening Wiisichong
results.content: The Secretary General of the Pan African Youth Union, Ahmed Bening Wiisichong has called for stronger financing, technical support and policy interventions to help young African innovators transform climate solutions into sustainable businesses capable of driving economic growth and job creation.

results.content: A 29-year-old Ghanaian fisherman has recounted how he and six colleagues survived nearly two weeks at sea after their canoe’s outboard motor broke down, leaving them without adequate food and drinking water.

results.content: The Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) is intensifying its nationwide public education campaign on Ghana’s impending ban on polystyrene foam products, taking the campaign to five northern regions as the January 1, 2027, implementation deadline approaches.

results.title: The betrayal of the ones we trusted
results.content: There is a loneliness that has nothing to do with being alone. It is the loneliness of knocking on the door of the institution that was built for you, and hearing only the echo.

results.content: The tournament featured competitive men’s and women’s wheelchair tennis divisions, providing athletes with an opportunity to showcase their skills, resilience and sportsmanship.

results.title: MUSIGA warns musicians against glorifying online fraud
results.content: The Musicians Union of Ghana (MUSIGA) has cautioned musicians against making public statements that could be interpreted as encouraging or glorifying online fraud and other cyber-related crimes.

results.title: Mahama describes AfCFTA as Africa’s ‘greatest architecture for conflict prevention’
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama has called for deeper economic integration among African countries, describing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) as a major instrument for preventing conflict and strengthening peaceful relations across the continent.

results.title: Africa needs stronger digital payment links to unlock regional trade – Femi Osinbajo
results.content: Professor Yemi Osinbajo, a former Vice-President of Nigeria, has called for stronger cooperation among African countries to improve cross-border payments, strengthen digital integration and support trade and investment across the continent.

results.title: Africa must prove climate adaptation is saving lives, not just spending money
results.content: When floods leave roads impassable, water supplies become contaminated and children fall ill, the consequences of climate change are measured in more than damaged infrastructure or financial losses. They are measured in lives disrupted, household incomes lost and families struggling to cope. For Dr Richard Munang, Director of the United Nations University Institute for Natural Resources in Africa (UNU-INRA), these are the realities that must shape how Africa measures progress on climate adaptation.

results.title: PIAC seeks details of petroleum funds allocated to Big Push projects
results.content: The Public Interest and Accountability Committee (PIAC) released its 2026 semi-annual report on Ghana’s petroleum revenue management, noting that additional information on how the government uses petroleum revenues allocated to the national budget would strengthen its assessment of government expenditure.

results.title: NRSA praises Sunyani inner ring road project, raises concern over tricycle speeding
results.content: The National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) in the Bono Region has lauded the quality of work on the Sunyani-Inner Ring Road Project, being funded by the government's “Big Push” Road Infrastructure programme.

results.title: Mahama warns foreign powers against treating Africa as a ‘chessboard’
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama has urged African leaders to unite against foreign interference and protect the continent’s sovereignty, warning that external powers are seeking strategic influence and access to Africa’s resources.

results.title: GES, stakeholders call for stronger action against child marriage in Eastern Region

results.title: NDC to investigate vote-buying allegations in constituency elections if evidence is provided
results.content: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) says it is prepared to investigate allegations of vote-buying in its ongoing constituency elections if credible evidence is brought before the party’s national executives.

results.title: Transport Minister calls for efficient, competitive ports to boost regional trade
results.content: Joseph Bukari Nikpe, the Minister for Transport, has called for improved port efficiency, digitalisation and stronger transport connectivity to position Ghana as a leading trade and logistics gateway for West Africa. Mr Nikpe said achieving the ambition required sustained collaboration among the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA), the government, private-sector operators, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders across the transport and logistics value chain. He made the call in a keynote address at the GPHA’s 40th Anniversary Dinner and Industry Awards, where he highlighted six priorities for building a more efficient, competitive, and sustainable port system. results.title: GoldBod begins stakeholder consultations ahead of 2027 small-scale mining support programme
results.content: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has begun engaging industry stakeholders on a proposed programme to formalise artisanal and small-scale mining and provide financial support to eligible operators ahead of its planned launch in 2027.

results.title: Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
results.content: Nearly 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people took part in another day of protests across France which were followed by some clashes late on Saturday, officials have said. After a day of largely peaceful demonstrations, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in a number of cities including Paris, while barricades were set alight in Marseille and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux. But officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, which resulted in some of the worst scenes of disorder in France's modern history. The interior ministry said an estimated 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while the unions put the number at about 800,000. Some 70,000 police officers were deployed and restrictions imposed in several cities to prevent the latest protests over the cost of living and poor school c

results.title: Tinubu blames opposition for hunger, poverty in Nigeria; Atiku kicks, says president delusional
results.content: President Bola Tinubu has accused opposition politicians of causing the hunger and poverty Nigerians are experiencing, insisting that his administration is working to address the problems as he formally launched his 2027 presidential campaign in Kaduna on Saturday. Mr Tinubu made the remarks at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign flag-off at Ranchers Bees Stadium (also known as Kaduna Township Stadium), ahead of the 2027 general elections. I have heard the opposition talking about hunger and poverty. Who caused them? They did! They caused hunger and poverty. We are trying to eliminate them,” the president said. He also urged his supporters to be wary of statements from the opposition, particularly criticism of his decision to remove the petrol subsidy, insisting that the country would not return to the previous system.

results.title: Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections
results.content: Former President Barack Obama has attacked the Trump administration over the Iran war and high consumer prices as he hit the campaign trail for Democrats ahead of the US midterm elections. "This election is our last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration," Obama told crowds in Ohio on Saturday. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump touted his administration's immigration and tariff policies at a rally in Georgia, telling supporters "we're in the golden age of America". The midterm elections on 3 November will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump's term, and therefore how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans.

results.title: Luv FM journalists sweep top honours at GJA Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards
results.content: Journalists from Luv FM, a subsidiary of the Multimedia Group Limited, have won multiple awards at the 2025 Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards. Four journalists from the Kumasi-based station received honours across several categories, with Emmanuel Bright Quaicoe taking the night's top prize as Ashanti Regional Journalist of the Year. Mr Quaicoe also won Best Feature Production, Best Agriculture Reporter, and placed second in Best Entertainment Journalism. Clinton Yeboah secured first place in both Best Health Journalism and Best Business and Economy Journalism.

results.title: Multimedia’s Emmanuel Bright Quaicoe wins 2025 GJA Ashanti Regional Journalist of the Year award
results.content: Luv FM journalist, Emmanuel Bright Quaicoe, has been crowned the 2025 Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Ashanti Regional Journalist of the Year, the highest individual honour at the regional media excellence awards. His award was announced at the GJA Ashanti Media Excellence Awards, which recognises outstanding journalistic work across the region. Mr Quaicoe secured three additional honours on the night, winning Best Feature Production, Best in Agriculture reporting and placing second in Best Entertainment Journalism.

results.title: Gizela Tetteh-Agbotui confident NDC will retain Awutu Senya West parliamentary seat
results.content: The Member of Parliament for Awutu Senya West, Gizela Tetteh-Agbotui, says she is confident the National Democratic Congress (NDC) will retain the constituency in the next general election, despite the election of an NPP regional chairman from the area. Dr Kwabena Essibu, who hails from Senya Breku in the constituency, was recently elected Central Regional chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP). During the NDC constituency executive elections, Ms Tetteh-Agbotui dismissed concerns that Dr Essibu’s election could improve the NPP’s chances of winning the parliamentary seat. She said the NDC would continue working to protect the seat, which she described as an important electoral hold for the party. Ms Tetteh-Agbotui disclosed that she had personally congratulated Dr Essibu on his election but told him she was determined to retain the constituency for the NDC.

results.title: All 24 NDC constituency executive positions in Juaboso go unopposed
results.content: All 24 constituency executive positions of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Juaboso have gone unopposed, with no contest required for any of the positions. The Member of Parliament for Juaboso, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, announced the outcome in a Facebook post on Saturday, October 24, congratulating the executives on their uncontested selection.
